description: In this seminar, we'll explore the evolution and manifestations of how society has tried to control and shape our environment and the spaces we live in--from suburbs to the planning of major cities to what makes an area like Division Street in Northfield difficult to replicate. How has this obsession with placemaking (including our digital streets) impacted our conception of family, work, and community? How has the organization of our neighborhoods contributed to racism and socio-economic divides? Major assignments will include personal narratives and reflective journals, an op-ed, a creative project centering around town/city planning, and a major research essay.
